title: Enhancement: PDDF CHILD_CARDS Support
author: antonio-nexthop
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the enhancement

PDDF currently instantiates devices during boot using the hard-coded `dev_type` attribute. This enhancement adds the ability to initialize component whose instantiation depends on information read from an EEPROM. This is useful for instance, if a component is sourced from multiple vendors and consequently has a different interface / driver depending on which vendor/model is loaded on a given system.

https://github.com/sonic-net/SONiC/pull/2494

### Current Behavior

PDDF instantiates devices during boot using the hard-coded `dev_type` attribute

### Proposed Behavior

PDDF supports ability to instantiate different devices based on content read from an EEPROM

-->

#### Why I did it

PDDF currently instantiates devices during boot using the hard-coded `dev_type` attribute. This enhancement adds the ability to initialize component whose instantiation depends on information read from an EEPROM. This is useful for instance, if a component is sourced from multiple vendors and consequently has a different interface / driver depending on which vendor/model is loaded on a given system.

Associated HLD: https://github.com/sonic-net/SONiC/pull/2494
Resolves: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/28959

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**: 

#### How I did it

  - Added `expand_child_cards()` to `pddfparse`: at boot, for each `CHILD_CARDS` entry it decodes the identifying EEPROM via a platform hook, selects the matching per-variant fragment, and merges it (renumbering sensors) into `pddf-device.json` / `platform.json`. No-op when `CHILD_CARDS` is absent.
  - Added a vendor override surface `PddfPlatformHooks.decode_eeprom` (+ `ChildCardEepromUnprogrammed`) in
  `sonic-platform-pddf-base`, keeping the EEPROM decode platform-specific while `pddfparse` stays vendor-neutral.

Example usage of this feature: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/28988


#### How to verify it

Validated the feature on Nexthop platforms. See https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/28988 for details

This is useful for instance, if a component is sourced from multiple vendors and consequently has a different interface / driver depending on which vendor/model is loaded on a given system.

PDDF changes PR: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/28958
Resolves: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/28959

# Example Usage
The `CHILD_CARDS` feature is used by the Nexthop NH-4220 platform:
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/28988

linkedPullRequests.title: [Nexthop] Add CHILD_CARDS support to NH-4220 platform
linkedPullRequests.author: antonio-nexthop
linkedPullRequests.body:
<!--
     Please make sure you've read and understood our contributing guidelines:
     https://github.com/Azure/SONiC/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md

     ** Make sure all your commits include a signature generated with `git commit -s` **

     If this is a bug fix, make sure your description includes "fixes #xxxx", or
     "closes #xxxx" or "resolves #xxxx"

     Please provide the following information:
-->

#### Why I did it

We would like to onboard the NH-4220 platform to the newly added PDDF `CHILD_CARDS` feature

Relevant PR with PDDF changes: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/28958
Resolves: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/28959

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it

- We define a new schema in `pddf-device.json`
```
  "CHILD_CARDS": {
    "FERN1": {
      "eeprom_device": "POWER-DELIVERY-CARD-EEPROM",
      "decoder":       "fern.v1",
      "slot":          0,
      "dev_addr":      "0x60",
      "parent":        "CPLDMUX0",
      "parent_chan":   "2",
      "parent_bus":    "0x53",
      "variants": [
        { "match": {"vendor": "DELTA", "model": "Q54SW120A7"},
          "pddf_json": "fern/delta_q54sw120a7.json.j2" },
        { "match": {"vendor": "BELF",  "model": "TQNM0M12B"},
          "pddf_json": "fern/belf_tqnm0m12b.json.j2"  }
      ]
    },
...
}
```

- `decoder` maps to a vendor specific function to decode EEPROMs. Vendors implement this by overriding a generic `PddfPlatformHooks.decode_eeprom` interface function

- Renamed `platform.json` to `platform.json.base` in source

Boot flow is now:

`pre_pddf_init.sh`:
  - Copy `pddf-device.json.base` to `pddf-device.json`

`pddfparse` runs

`pddf_post_device_create.sh`:
 - expands `CHILD_CARDS`
   - This step reads the EEPROM to determine vendor/model information
   - picks the correct fragment of PDDF configuration to load
   - splices in the devices into `pddf-device.json` and `platform.json`
   - creates relevant devices

#### How to verify it

Validated on Nexthop platforms:

- On supported platform with PDC EEPROM programmed, `CHILD_CARDS` devices correctly detected, `pddf-device.json` shows expanded `CHILD_CARDS` entries. `pddf-device.json.base` remains at pre-expansion state. `test_thermal.py` passing, validating `platform.json`
- On supported platform with PDC EEPROM **unprogrammed**, `CHILD_CARDS` devices missing, but DUT behaves the same way otherwise
- On unsupported platform with no `CHILD_CARDS` defined, no behaviour change
